QG.ENGINEERING.title: PQCensus evidence and abstention policy
QG.ENGINEERING.notes: Tool behavior, not an external cryptographic standard. It is explicitly separated from NIST and other authorities.

NIST.FIPS.203.title: Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Standard
NIST.FIPS.203.notes: Final standard. NIST posted a 2025 planning note identifying potential errata for a future update.

NIST.FIPS.204.title: Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard
NIST.FIPS.204.notes: Final standard. Consult the current NIST publication page for errata planning notes.

NIST.FIPS.205.title: Stateless Hash-Based Digital Signature Standard
NIST.FIPS.205.notes: Final standard. Additional limited-use parameter sets remain separate draft work and are not treated as final here.

NIST.SP.800-227.title: Recommendations for Key-Encapsulation Mechanisms
NIST.SP.800-227.notes: Final recommendations for securely implementing and using KEMs.

NIST.IR.8547.IPD.title: Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards
NIST.IR.8547.IPD.notes: Draft transition guidance. It is not represented as a final NIST standard.

NIST.SP.800-57.title: Recommendation for Key Management
NIST.SP.800-57.notes: General key-management guidance; PQCensus does not treat it as a purpose-specific PQC replacement table.

rules.recommendation: Migrate the signature workflow to ML-DSA or SLH-DSA after protocol and certificate compatibility review.
rules.interpretation: PQCensus maps verified signature usage to signature-class PQC candidates. Severity and deployment ordering are PQCensus engineering judgments, not NIST certification.

rules.recommendation: Migrate key establishment or key transport to ML-KEM or a supported hybrid protocol transition; do not substitute a signature algorithm.
rules.interpretation: PQCensus maps verified encryption or key-establishment usage to KEM-class candidates. Neutral-context findings are high severity; supplied exposure, confidentiality lifetime, and HNDL context can raise urgency to critical. Severity is PQCensus engineering guidance.

rules.recommendation: Plan a certificate and signature migration to ML-DSA or SLH-DSA with verifier rollout before issuer changes.
rules.interpretation: PQCensus treats ECDSA as a signature primitive and preserves PKI/verifier constraints. Severity and urgency are tool judgments.

rules.recommendation: Use a protocol-aware hybrid transition candidate combining classical and ML-KEM key establishment before retiring ECDH.
rules.interpretation: PQCensus treats ECDH as key agreement and recommends protocol-aware KEM transition planning, not an algorithm-name substitution.

rules.recommendation: Assess a protocol-supported hybrid key-establishment transition using ML-KEM; X25519 is not a signature and must not map to ML-DSA.
rules.interpretation: PQCensus treats X25519 as key agreement and preserves negotiation and peer-compatibility unknowns.

rules.recommendation: Assess a protocol-supported hybrid key-establishment transition using ML-KEM; X448 is not a signature and must not map to ML-DSA.
rules.interpretation: PQCensus treats X448 as a distinct key-agreement primitive and preserves negotiation and peer-compatibility unknowns.

rules.recommendation: Assess a protocol-supported hybrid transition to ML-KEM before retiring finite-field Diffie-Hellman.
rules.interpretation: PQCensus treats finite-field DH as key agreement and requires protocol-aware migration planning.

rules.recommendation: Plan a verifier-first signature migration to ML-DSA or SLH-DSA; preserve certificate and software-signing compatibility constraints.
rules.interpretation: PQCensus treats EdDSA families as signatures and retains verifier and certificate compatibility as unresolved deployment context.

rules.recommendation: Record parameter set, protocol support, implementation validation, and fallback policy.
rules.interpretation: Detection of an ML-KEM name records availability or configuration only; PQCensus does not infer validated deployment or interoperability.

rules.recommendation: Record parameter set, verifier rollout, certificate profile, and key lifecycle controls.
rules.interpretation: Detection of an ML-DSA name records availability or configuration only; PQCensus does not infer validation, key protection, or verifier rollout.

rules.recommendation: Record parameter set and signature-size/performance constraints before deployment.
rules.interpretation: Detection of an SLH-DSA name records availability or configuration only; performance, parameter-set, and deployment constraints remain explicit.

rules.recommendation: Do not treat ordinary SHA-256 use as equivalent to a Shor-vulnerable public-key finding; review output length and lifecycle requirements.
rules.interpretation: PQCensus classifies supported SHA-2/SHA-3 observations as non-Shor findings. Any lifecycle advice is an engineering interpretation, not a claim that SHA-256 is broken.

rules.recommendation: Review key length and lifecycle; no blanket PQ replacement is implied by this finding.
rules.interpretation: PQCensus classifies HMAC as a symmetric MAC and does not issue a blanket PQ replacement recommendation.

rules.recommendation: Replace the legacy or deprecated TLS protocol selection before planning post-quantum protocol migration.
rules.interpretation: Legacy TLS protocol constants (SSLv2/SSLv3/TLSv1/TLSv1.1) and deprecated wrappers such as ssl.wrap_socket are insecure baseline configurations. This finding is separate from classical-key-agreement migration findings.

rules.recommendation: Restore certificate validation (default context) before planning any protocol-level migration.
rules.interpretation: Explicitly disabling certificate validation (check_hostname=False, CERT_NONE) is an insecure configuration distinct from protocol age or key-agreement class.

rules.recommendation: Resolve the cryptographic purpose and runtime/protocol context before selecting any migration target.
rules.interpretation: This is an explicit abstention rule. It must not be represented as NIST guidance and never maps an unknown purpose to a PQC primitive.
